# omx-dsp / fuzz_eq

omx-dsp's own fuzz target `fuzz_eq` ([source](source/fuzz_eq.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over omx-dsp 0.27.0 (FreeMixer/omx-dsp at a0ee1dfe).

Reads a rate (from the oracle grid or any rate from 8 to 768 kHz) and designs the head high-pass and low-pass from raw double corners. It then reads 1 to 24 bands, each with a kind, an on switch, a raw double corner and Q, and a gain within +-24 dB or exactly 0, and designs the bank. It evaluates the bank's magnitude at four frequencies, runs a finite block of 1 to 255 samples through the mono or stereo cascade, and calls the two bandwidth-to-Q conversions.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against libomxdsp.a, which build.sh compiles from omx-dsp's five src/*.c files with -DOMX_CONTRACTS and -ffp-contract=off; the EQ design, biquad and magnitude code is inline in the headers. The Makefile's own fuzz build uses native clang with libFuzzer, which this build replaces with the standard driver.
- omx-contract's headers are pinned to the tag v3.4.0 (1169c701), where the library's Makefile uses whichever omx-contract is installed, at or above its packaging floor of 3.1.0.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- The head filters write at most four sections. Each section is stable (Jury conditions, computed by the harness) and has finite numerator coefficients ([lines 86-100](source/fuzz_eq.c#L86-L100)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The bank has at most as many sections as bands, exactly one per band that is on, and none when the EQ is off ([lines 118-131](source/fuzz_eq.c#L118-L131)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Every section of the bank is stable by the harness's own reading of its coefficients, and every coefficient is finite ([lines 135-149](source/fuzz_eq.c#L135-L149)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Section i belongs to the i-th band that is on. It is parked exactly when that band is a peaking or shelf band at 0 dB, and its gain at DC matches the band kind's closed form to a relative tolerance of 1e-3 ([lines 153-169](source/fuzz_eq.c#L153-L169)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The bank's magnitude in dB is finite at every frequency asked, and it is exactly 0 dB when no section is live ([lines 177-192](source/fuzz_eq.c#L177-L192)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The cascade gives finite samples for finite samples. A bank with no live section leaves the block unchanged, bit for bit, on each leg it runs ([lines 208-229](source/fuzz_eq.c#L208-L229)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The bandwidth-to-Q conversion gives a finite Q that is not negative for any finite width above 0. The octaves-to-Q conversion gives a finite positive Q for any finite width ([lines 237-252](source/fuzz_eq.c#L237-L252)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- After each stage, no contract of the library is recorded as broken. rate-is-declared is skipped at a rate that is not declared ([lines 160-168](source/fuzz.h#L160-L168)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
